dedupe_keys.name: mosaik smart grid co simulation framework

description: mosaik is a co-simulation framework with an emphasis on smart grid simulation, developed by the mosaik team at OFFIS. It lets users reuse and combine existing simulators to build large-scale smart grid scenarios, with thousands of simulated entities distributed over several simulator processes, and use them as test beds for control strategies such as multi-agent systems or centralised control. A scenario API starts simulator processes, instantiates models and connects entities one by one or by probability distributions; a simulator manager starts processes or connects to running instances; and coordinated execution combines time-based and event-based stepping so each simulator can use its own step size. The mosaik API integrates simulators and controllers written in any programming language. It is written in Python and fully open source under the LGPL, with simple simulators, bindings to network calculation tools such as PYPOWER and pandapower and a demonstration scenario; the latest release announced was 3.7.0 and the last commit read was 28 August 2026. Coverage is general. Caveats: mosaik coordinates simulators but does not itself model grid physics, and the current code requires Python 3.12 or later. Simulation uses are co-simulation of power grids with control, communication and market agents for resilience and control strategy tests. Related records: platform-helics is another co-simulation framework.
